INTERNATIONAL ISLAMIC UNIVERSITY MALAYSIA
                                DRESS CODE


In  exercise  of  the  powers  conferred  by  Article  40  (1)  (e)  of  the
Constitution  of  the  International  Islamic  University  Malaysia,  the
Board of Governors makes the following code:



                                    PART 1

                              PRELIMINARY

Citation

1.   This code may be cited as the International Islamic University
     Malaysia Dress Code, and may be referred to as “IIUM Dress
     Code”.

Application

2.   IIUM Dress Code shall apply to every student and staff of the
     University.



Interpretation

3.    In this IIUM Dress Code, interpretation made by the University
in relation to the IIUM Dress Code shall be final and conclusive unless
the context otherwise requires:


                                                                   P a g e 5 | 27

A  reference  to  any  statute  or  legislation  shall,  unless  otherwise
indicated, be a reference to the statute or legislation of Malaysia and
includes  any  statutory  modification,  amendment  or  re-enactment
thereof;

Reference to “Islam” and “Shariah” shall, unless otherwise indicated,
bear the same meaning herein;

All schedules, attachments, notice, standing order, publication and
annexure hereto form part of the IIUM Dress Code;


                                     PART II

                               GENERAL CODE

Display of the University’s identification card.

4.    Staff  and  students  shall  display  their  respective  University’s
identification cards at all material times whilst in the University’s
premises  except  when  attending  non-formal  activities,  sports  and
outdoor activities.

Approved attire

5.    (1)    Staff  and     students  shall  dress  in  accordance  with  the
approved attire by the University as illustrated in Appendix A of the
IIUM Dress Code.

                                                                       P a g e 9 | 27

(2)    Staff and students shall not wear any attires which have
provocative or detrimental designs, images, words or phrases that is
against the IIUM Dress Code.

      (3)    Staff and students are not allowed to wear any attires which
symbolise any particular external organisation or group except on
certain proper occasions and with the permission from the University
Authority.


Attire must cover the aurah

6.    (1)    The attire of a male in public must be reasonably decent in
accordance with the urf (local custom) and shall cover the aurah of the
male body except under permissible circumstances such as sporting
events and in the Mahallah room.

      (2)    A female Muslim attire should cover the whole body save
for the face and the palm.

      (3)    A female Non-Muslim may adopt Islamic dress, if she so
desires, or at least cover the head with a scarf or shawl or similar
headgear as a symbol of respect to the Islamic university.




                                                                    P a g e 10 | 27

Formal dressing

7.     (1)    Staff shall wear approved office attire during the working
hours, other official University functions and other formal activities

      (2)     Students  may  wear  shirts  and  collared  T-shirts  when
attending classes and the shirts and collared T-shirts shall at all material
times be tucked in the trousers.

Notwithstanding the above, the Kulliyyah may determine the proper
attire for the students in accordance with the specific requirement of
the disciplines of studies.

       (3)    Slippers, non-strip sandals, round neck T-shirts, tight-fitting
trousers including jeans or pants should not be worn by students during
lectures,  tutorials,  official  University  functions  and  other  formal
activities as well as within the proximity of IIUM administrative and
faculty buildings and centres.


National dress

8.     Staff and students are encouraged to wear complete national
dresses/attires provided that they do not violate or infringe the IIUM
Dress Code and Islamic values and norms.



                                                                       P a g e 11 | 27

Cross dressing

9.     Staff and students are not allowed to wear dresses, accessories or
cosmetic products which resemble the opposite gender.



Accessories and jewelleries

10.    (1)    Staff and students shall not display excessive accessories,
apply excessive cosmetic products and use strong perfumes.

      (2)     Staff and students are not allowed to wear any accessories,
which symbolise any particular external organisation or group except
on  certain  proper  occasions  and  with  the  permission  from  the
University Authority.

      (3)     No  male  shall      wear  necklace  and  bracelet  except  for
medical purposes and identification or on religious and/or traditional
grounds.


Ceremonial attire

11.    Save as for convocation, the ceremonial attire for graduands, shall
be such as determined by the University from time to time.



                                                                      P a g e 12 | 27

Trousers

12.    (1)    Males  are  allowed  to  wear  jeans  during  non-formal
activities and during physical activities such as sports or recreation,
provided that they are not tight-fitting, multi-coloured, faded, and fancy
in design, torn or with patches.

       (2)    Females  may wear loose  pants  which cover the ankles
provided that the pants are worn with long, loose upper dresses, which
cover the hip. Tight-fitting or figure-hugging pants are not allowed to
be worn except in the Mahallah room.

Upper dress and blouse

13.    A female staff and student may wear a loose-fitting blouse and
upper dress provided that the items do not have long slits or side cuts
which reveal the hips or thigh area, the length covers the hips and the
sleeves are long enough reaching the wrists.


Hairstyles

14.    (1)    The length of the hair of a male shall not extend beyond the
collar and the hairdo should not be of unusual or extraordinary style.

      (2)      Staff and students are prohibited to dye or colour his or her
   hair unnecessarily.

                                                                      P a g e 13 | 27

Head-cover and men headwear

15.   (1)    A female Muslim is required to wear a proper head-cover
which serves the purpose of covering the aurah.

      (2)    A non-Muslim female is required to cover her head with a
scarf or shawl or similar headgear when she is in the University or
outside the University when she is representing the University in any
formal or informal activities.

      (3)    Male staff and students shall not wear hats or caps whilst
attending official and formal functions  except on religious  and/or
traditional grounds.


Footwear

16.   (1)    Staff must wear proper office shoes during working hours,
official University functions and other formal activities.

                                   PENALTY


Compound

shall be subjected to a compound for a sum of Ringgit                    Malaysia
Hundred (RM100.00) for each offence under this Code.

fourteen (14) days from the date of its issuance.

rules.titleOriginal: Disciplinary liability of office-bearers, etc. of a student organisation, body or group

49. (1) Where any disciplinary misconduct has been committed
under the IIUM SDR, whether or not any student has been found guilty
in respect thereof, and such disciplinary misconduct has been
committed or purports to have been committed in the name or on behalf
of any organisation, body or group of students of the University which
is established by, under or in accordance with the Constitution, or any
other organisation, body or group of students of the University, every
office-bearer of such organisation, body or group and every student
managing or assisting in the management of such organisation, body or
group at the time of the commission of such disciplinary misconduct
shall be deemed to be guilty of such disciplinary misconduct and shall
be liable to punishment therefore, unless he establishes to the
satisfaction of the appropriate Disciplinary Authority that the
disciplinary misconduct was committed without his knowledge and
that he had exercised all due diligence to prevent the commission of the
disciplinary misconduct.
(2) Any office-bearer of, or any student managing or assisting
in the management of, any organisation, body or group as referred to in
sub-rule (1) shall be liable to be proceeded against under this rule,



notwithstanding that he may not have taken part in the commission of
the disciplinary misconduct.
(3) In any disciplinary proceeding under this rule against any
office bearer of, or any student managing or assisting in the
management of, any organisation, body or group, any document found
in the possession of any office-bearer of, or person managing or
assisting in the management of, such organisation, body or group, or in
the possession of a member of such organisation, body or group, shall
be prima facie evidence of the contents thereof for the purpose of
proving that anything has been done or purports to have been done by
or on behalf of such organisation, body or group.
rules.summaryZh: 以学生组织名义违规时，负责人及管理协助者可承担责任；原文列有不知情且已尽责的抗辩条件。

approved attire by the University as illustrated in Appendix A of the

provocative or detrimental designs, images, words or phrases that is

6. (1) The attire of a male in public must be reasonably decent in
accordance with the urf (local custom) and shall cover the aurah of the
male body except under permissible circumstances such as sporting
events and in the Mahallah room.

(2) A female Muslim attire should cover the whole body save
for the face and the palm.

(3) A female Non-Muslim may adopt Islamic dress, if she so
desires, or at least cover the head with a scarf or shawl or similar
headgear as a symbol of respect to the Islamic university.
rules.summaryZh: 男性公共场所着装须得体并遮蔽 aurah，运动及宿舍房间等有例外；穆斯林女性除脸及手掌外覆盖身体，非穆斯林女性另有头部覆盖说明。

7. (1) Staff shall wear approved office attire during the working
hours, other official University functions and other formal activities

(2) Students may wear shirts and collared T-shirts when
attending classes and the shirts and collared T-shirts shall at all material
times be tucked in the trousers.

Notwithstanding the above, the Kulliyyah may determine the proper
attire for the students in accordance with the specific requirement of
the disciplines of studies.

(3) Slippers, non-strip sandals, round neck T-shirts, tight-fitting
trousers including jeans or pants should not be worn by students during
lectures, tutorials, official University functions and other formal
activities as well as within the proximity of IIUM administrative and
faculty buildings and centres.

dresses/attires provided that they do not violate or infringe the IIUM

17. (1) Any person who contravenes any provision of this Code
shall be subjected to a compound for a sum of Ringgit Malaysia
Hundred (RM100.00) for each offence under this Code.

(2) A compound issued under this Code shall be paid within
fourteen (14) days from the date of its issuance.

(3) A compound issued under this Code shall be dealt with in
accordance with the compound procedures made by the University.

(4) Any reduction of a compound issued under this Code shall
be decided by the relevant Executive Personnel.

rules.originalText:
23. (1) It is the responsibility of an organiser to inform participants
and invited guests on the observance of the IIUM Dress Code.
Information of the same shall be reflected in all invitation letters/cards,
posters including electronic posters and brochures. Failure to adhere to
this provision, the Person- in- Charge or the Director of the Programme
shall be subjected to a compound, unless he establishes to the
satisfaction of the appropriate University Authority that the misconduct
was committed without his knowledge and that he had exercised all due
diligence to prevent the commission of the misconduct.

(2) Any office bearer of, or any student or staff managing or
assisting in the management of, any organisation, body or group as
referred to in sub-rule (1) shall be liable to be proceeded against under
this rule, notwithstanding that he may not have taken part in the
commission of the misconduct.
